content_en.val: Bullish / Bearish
Bullish means expecting prices to go up. Bearish means expecting prices to go down.
Stop Loss (SL)
An order placed to close a losing position to prevent further losses.
Take Profit (TP)
An order to close a profitable position once it reaches a specific target.
Risk/Reward Ratio (RR)
The ratio between the potential loss (risk) and potential gain (reward) of a trade.
Timeframe
The candle interval used to read the market. Shorter timeframes change faster and contain more noise; longer timeframes describe broader structure.
Support / Resistance
Price areas where buying or selling pressure has repeatedly appeared. They are zones, not guaranteed reversal points.
Fundamental Context
News, policy, and economic-event context that may change volatility or market direction beyond the chart alone.
Bullish / Bearish / Neutral Bias
The direction favored by current evidence. Neutral means the evidence is mixed or not strong enough to favor either side.
Signal Strength / Confidence
Signal strength summarizes directional clarity. Confidence summarizes support from the available evidence; neither is a guaranteed win probability.
Validity / Invalidation / Expired
Validity is the intended use window. Invalidation is a condition that cancels the scenario. Expired means its time window has ended.
Standard Plan / Preferred Side / Wait
The Standard Plan groups both directional scenarios. Preferred Side is the better-supported one; Wait means immediate execution is not supported.
Adaptive Position Plan / Layer
An account-aware calculation with manual staged checkpoints. A layer is a possible addition that must be reassessed, not an automatic order.
Margin / Margin Call / Liquidation
Margin is collateral for an open position. Margin call and liquidation thresholds are account controls defined by the displayed rules.
Spread / Fee / Rollover / Slippage
Trading costs and execution effects that can make the realized outcome differ from a simple entry-to-exit price calculation.
Timeframe Risk Map / Relative Risk
A comparison of technical risk among available timeframe snapshots. Relative risk only ranks the compared options; lower does not mean risk-free.
BUY / SELL / Both
Chart visibility controls for the BUY scenario, SELL scenario, or both scenarios together. They do not place an order or change the analysis.
Running Price
The latest available reference price shown on the chart. It can move after the saved analysis levels were created.
XP / Level / Rank / Mastery
XP records verified discipline activity. XP advances Levels 1–100 and their Ranks; after level 100, continued progress is recorded as Mastery.
Achievement Badge / Streak / XP History
A badge marks a discipline milestone, a streak counts consistent active days, and XP History lists verified XP events. All are private and are not measures of profit or trading skill.

content_id.val: Bullish / Bearish
Bullish berarti perkiraan harga akan naik. Bearish berarti perkiraan harga akan turun.
Stop Loss (SL)
Order untuk menutup posisi yang rugi demi mencegah kerugian lebih lanjut.
Take Profit (TP)
Order untuk menutup posisi untung setelah mencapai target tertentu.
Risk/Reward Ratio (RR)
Rasio antara potensi kerugian (risiko) dan potensi keuntungan (reward) dari sebuah trade.
Timeframe
Interval candle yang dipakai untuk membaca market. Timeframe pendek berubah lebih cepat dan lebih banyak noise; timeframe panjang menggambarkan struktur yang lebih luas.
Support / Resistance
Area harga tempat tekanan beli atau jual berulang kali muncul. Ini merupakan zona, bukan titik pembalikan yang dijamin.
Konteks Fundamental
Konteks berita, kebijakan, dan agenda ekonomi yang dapat mengubah volatilitas atau arah market di luar pembacaan chart.
Bias Bullish / Bearish / Netral
Arah yang lebih didukung bukti saat ini. Netral berarti buktinya campuran atau belum cukup kuat untuk memilih salah satu sisi.
Signal Strength / Confidence
Signal strength merangkum kejelasan arah. Confidence merangkum dukungan bukti yang tersedia; keduanya bukan peluang menang yang dijamin.
Validity / Invalidation / Expired
Validity adalah jendela penggunaan. Invalidation adalah kondisi pembatal skenario. Expired berarti jendela waktunya sudah selesai.
Standard Plan / Sisi Pilihan / Tunggu
Standard Plan mengelompokkan dua skenario arah. Sisi Pilihan adalah yang lebih didukung; Tunggu berarti eksekusi segera belum didukung.
Adaptive Position Plan / Layer
Kalkulasi sesuai kondisi akun dengan checkpoint bertahap manual. Layer adalah opsi penambahan yang harus dinilai ulang, bukan order otomatis.
Margin / Margin Call / Likuidasi
Margin adalah jaminan untuk posisi terbuka. Batas margin call dan likuidasi adalah kontrol akun dari aturan yang ditampilkan.
Spread / Fee / Rollover / Slippage
Biaya dan efek eksekusi yang dapat membuat hasil nyata berbeda dari kalkulasi sederhana harga entry ke exit.
Peta Risiko Timeframe / Risiko Relatif
Perbandingan risiko teknikal antar-snapshot timeframe yang tersedia. Risiko relatif hanya mengurutkan pilihan yang dibandingkan; lebih rendah bukan berarti bebas risiko.
BUY / SELL / Keduanya
Kontrol tampilan chart untuk melihat skenario BUY, skenario SELL, atau keduanya sekaligus. Kontrol ini tidak memasang order dan tidak mengubah analisis.
Running Price
Harga acuan terbaru yang tersedia pada chart. Nilainya dapat bergerak setelah level analisis tersimpan dibuat.
XP / Level / Rank / Mastery
XP mencatat aktivitas disiplin yang terverifikasi. XP menaikkan Level 1–100 beserta Rank; setelah level 100, progres berikutnya dicatat sebagai Mastery.
Achievement Badge / Streak / Riwayat XP
Badge menandai milestone disiplin, streak menghitung konsistensi hari aktif, dan Riwayat XP mencantumkan event XP terverifikasi. Semuanya pribadi dan bukan ukuran profit atau keahlian trading.

articles.title_en: FOMO — Trading Late on a Move
articles.title_id: FOMO — Telat Masuk Saat Harga Sudah Jalan
articles.summary_en: Why chasing breakouts hurts and how to wait for second chances.
articles.summary_id: Kenapa ngejar breakout sering buntung dan cara nunggu peluang kedua.

content_en.val: FOMO — Fear Of Missing Out — is the urge to enter a trade after the move has already started, because you're afraid the rest of the move will happen without you.
The problem: by the time the move is obvious enough to make you anxious, you're entering near the end of the impulse — exactly where smart money is taking profit.
What to do instead

val: Accept that you'll miss most moves — that's normal.
Wait for a pullback to a clear level (S/R, EMA, previous structure).
If no pullback comes, let the trade go. There will be another setup.
Write down 'I missed X today, but my plan said wait' — train the habit.

content_en.val: The market opens every day. A missed trade is not a lost trade — a forced trade is.

content_id.val: FOMO — Fear Of Missing Out — itu dorongan untuk masuk trade setelah harga sudah jalan, karena takut sisa pergerakannya akan terjadi tanpa kamu.
Masalahnya: saat pergerakannya sudah jelas banget sampai bikin kamu cemas, kamu masuk di akhir impulse — persis di titik smart money sedang ambil profit.
Yang harus dilakukan

val: Terima bahwa kamu akan ketinggalan kebanyakan pergerakan — itu wajar.
Tunggu pullback ke level jelas (S/R, EMA, struktur sebelumnya).
Kalau pullback nggak datang, lepas saja. Pasti ada setup lain.
Catat: 'Hari ini gw missed X, tapi planning gw bilang nunggu' — latih kebiasaannya.

content_id.val: Pasar buka tiap hari. Trade yang missed bukan trade yang rugi — trade yang dipaksa baru rugi.

articles.title_en: Revenge Trading — Trying to Win It Back
articles.summary_en: The most expensive emotion. Recognize it, then stop.
articles.summary_id: Emosi paling mahal di trading. Kenali, lalu stop.

content_en.val: Revenge trading is opening a new position right after a loss, with the goal of recovering the loss — not because your plan said so.
The size usually goes up. The setup quality usually goes down. The combination is how small losses become account-killing losses.
The rule

val: After 2 consecutive losses → 30-minute break, no chart.
After 3 losses in a day → close the platform, day is done.
Never increase position size to 'make it back'.
Tomorrow exists.

content_id.val: Revenge trading itu buka posisi baru langsung setelah loss, dengan tujuan nutup loss — bukan karena planning kamu bilang begitu.
Ukurannya biasanya naik. Kualitas setup biasanya turun. Kombinasi inilah yang bikin loss kecil jadi loss penghabis akun.
Aturannya

val: Setelah 2 loss berturut-turut → istirahat 30 menit, jauhi chart.
Setelah 3 loss dalam sehari → tutup platform, hari ini selesai.
Jangan pernah naikkan ukuran posisi buat 'nutup balik'.
Besok masih ada.

articles.title_en: Loss Aversion — Holding Losers Too Long
articles.summary_en: Why a -2% trade feels worse than a +2% trade feels good.
articles.summary_id: Kenapa loss -2% terasa lebih sakit daripada profit +2% terasa enak.

content_en.val: Humans feel the pain of a loss about 2x stronger than the pleasure of an equivalent gain. In trading this shows up as: cutting winners early, holding losers in the hope they 'come back'.
The hope-based hold turns a planned -1R loss into a -3R or -5R disaster. That single trade then needs 3-5 winning trades to recover.
The fix

val: Pre-set the stop-loss before entry. Not after.
Treat the SL as a fact, not an opinion you can change later.
If you keep moving SL further, you don't have a strategy — you have hope.
Smaller positions make it easier to accept the loss.

content_id.val: Manusia merasakan sakit kerugian sekitar 2x lebih kuat dari nikmatnya keuntungan setara. Di trading ini muncul sebagai: cut winner kepagian, nahan loser dengan harapan 'pasti balik'.
Holding berbasis harapan mengubah loss -1R yang sudah direncanakan jadi bencana -3R atau -5R. Trade itu butuh 3-5 trade profit buat balik modal.
Solusinya

val: Set stop-loss SEBELUM masuk. Bukan setelah.
Anggap SL itu fakta, bukan opini yang bisa kamu ubah belakangan.
Kalau kamu terus geser SL menjauh, kamu nggak punya strategi — kamu punya harapan.
Posisi yang lebih kecil bikin loss lebih mudah diterima.

articles.summary_en: Why your entry price matters less than you think.
articles.summary_id: Kenapa harga entry kamu nggak sepenting yang kamu kira.

content_en.val: Anchoring is sticking to a reference price — usually your entry, or yesterday's high — and refusing to act when current price says otherwise.
The market doesn't know your entry price. It moves based on what's happening now and what traders expect next. Holding because 'I'm only -0.5% down' is anchoring, not analysis.
Ask yourself: 'If I had no position right now, would I open this trade?' If no → close it.

content_id.val: Anchoring itu nempel ke harga referensi — biasanya harga entry kamu, atau high kemarin — dan menolak bertindak walau harga sekarang bilang sebaliknya.
Pasar nggak tau harga entry kamu. Dia bergerak berdasar apa yang terjadi sekarang dan ekspektasi trader berikutnya. Nahan karena 'kan baru -0.5%' itu anchoring, bukan analisis.
Tanya ke diri: 'Kalau gw lagi nggak punya posisi, gw bakal buka trade ini sekarang?' Kalau jawabannya nggak → tutup posisi.

articles.summary_en: Profit follows discipline. Discipline starts with size.
articles.summary_id: Profit ngikutin disiplin. Disiplin dimulai dari ukuran posisi.

content_en.val: Professional traders think in this order: 1) how much can I lose, 2) what's my entry, 3) what's my target. Beginners reverse it: 1) target, 2) entry, 3) — uh, stop?

The 1% rule: never risk more than 1% of your account on a single trade. With 1% risk per trade, you can lose 10 in a row and still have 90% of your capital. With 5% risk, 10 losses = you're at 60%, and need a +67% gain to recover.
Position size formula
Position size = (account × risk%) / (entry − stop-loss in price points × point value)
If the math gives you a smaller size than your minimum tradeable lot, skip the trade. The stop-loss is too far — wait for a tighter setup.

content_id.val: Trader profesional mikir dalam urutan ini: 1) berapa maksimal lossnya, 2) entry di mana, 3) target di mana. Pemula kebalik: 1) target, 2) entry, 3) — eh, stop?

Aturan 1%: jangan pernah risiko lebih dari 1% akun untuk satu trade. Dengan risk 1%, kamu bisa loss 10 kali beruntun dan masih punya 90% modal. Dengan risk 5%, 10 loss = sisa 60%, butuh +67% gain buat balik modal.
Rumus position size
Position size = (akun × risk%) / (entry − stop-loss dalam point harga × nilai per point)
Kalau hitungannya keluar ukuran lebih kecil dari minimum lot yang bisa ditradingkan, skip trade-nya. Stop-lossnya kejauhan — tunggu setup yang lebih ketat.

articles.title_en: Plan vs Prediction — You Don't Need to Be Right
articles.title_id: Planning vs Prediksi — Kamu Nggak Harus Bener
articles.summary_en: A good trader with a 40% win rate beats a 'guru' with 70%.
articles.summary_id: Trader bagus dengan win rate 40% mengalahkan 'guru' dengan win rate 70%.

content_en.val: Beginners think trading is about predicting where price will go. Pros know it's about managing the trade once it's open — when you're right AND when you're wrong.
With a 1:3 risk-reward ratio, you only need to be right 30% of the time to break even. With 1:5, only 18%. The edge isn't prediction — it's letting winners run further than losers.
Your job isn't to be right. Your job is to manage what happens after you click buy or sell.

content_id.val: Pemula kira trading itu soal prediksi harga akan ke mana. Pro tau ini soal manage trade setelah posisi terbuka — saat kamu bener DAN saat kamu salah.
Dengan risk-reward 1:3, kamu cuma perlu bener 30% buat break-even. Dengan 1:5, cuma 18%. Edge-nya bukan prediksi — tapi membiarkan profit lari lebih jauh dari loss.
Tugas kamu bukan bener. Tugas kamu adalah manage apa yang terjadi setelah klik buy atau sell.

articles.summary_en: What you don't measure, you can't improve.
articles.summary_id: Yang nggak kamu ukur, nggak bisa kamu perbaiki.

content_en.val: Every trade should be journaled with at least: instrument, timeframe, entry & exit reason, what you felt during the trade, and what you'd do differently. Three months of this and patterns emerge that no course can teach you.
Patterns the journal usually reveals

val: You make money on one specific setup — and lose on the other 4 you try.
You overtrade on Mondays (revenge from a bad weekend) or Fridays (closing for the week).
Your win rate is 60% on planned trades, 20% on impulse trades.
You move stops on trades opened after 9pm.

content_id.val: Tiap trade harus dijurnal minimal: instrument, timeframe, alasan entry & exit, apa yang kamu rasakan saat trade, dan apa yang akan kamu lakukan beda. Tiga bulan begini dan polanya keluar — pola yang nggak akan diajari kursus mana pun.
Pola yang biasa keluar dari jurnal

val: Kamu cuan di satu setup spesifik — dan loss di 4 setup lain yang kamu coba.
Kamu overtrading hari Senin (revenge weekend buruk) atau Jumat (mau tutup minggu).
Win rate kamu 60% di planned trade, 20% di impulse trade.
Kamu geser stop di trade yang dibuka setelah jam 9 malam.

articles.title_en: Patience — Doing Nothing Is a Trade
articles.title_id: Sabar — Diam Itu Juga Pilihan Trading
articles.summary_en: Sitting in cash is a position. The hardest one.
articles.summary_id: Tetap cash itu posisi. Posisi tersulit.

content_en.val: The market generates maybe 3-5 high-quality setups per week per instrument. The other 80% of the time it's chop — sideways noise where edge is near zero.
If you only trade the 20%, you win consistently. If you trade the 100%, the 80% chop bleeds your account dry while the 20% pays for it. Most beginners trade 100%.
A trader who places 3 trades per week and wins 60% earns more than one who places 30 trades per week and wins 50%. Boring beats busy.

content_id.val: Pasar menghasilkan mungkin 3-5 setup berkualitas tinggi per minggu per instrument. 80% sisanya itu chop — noise sideways di mana edge mendekati nol.
Kalau kamu cuma trading di 20% itu, kamu menang konsisten. Kalau kamu trading 100%, 80% chop ngehabisin akun sementara 20% yang bayarin. Mayoritas pemula trading 100%.
Trader yang masuk 3 trade per minggu dengan win rate 60% earning lebih dari yang masuk 30 trade per minggu dengan win rate 50%. Bosan kalahin sibuk.
